Consumer complaint narrative:
My name is XXXX XXXX. Sadly, I have learned that I am a victim of an elaborate and systematic NAVIENT scam to direct unsuspecting NAVIENT student loan borrowers to third party brokers to steer said student loan borrows into student loan forgiveness for a substantial upfront fee unbeknown to the student loan borrower. In this nefarious scheme, in my case, when a student loan borrower contacts NAVIENT 's customer service, the student loan borrower without their knowledge is automatically redirected to a third party broker under the guise that this third party broker is a representative of NAVIENT. 

Once connected to this third party broker, this individual does not identify himself/herself as a third party broker nor their intentions, but misrepresents themselves as NAVIENT representatives as they execute their scheme to convince student loan borrowers to allow the third party broker to file for student loan forgiveness as this is the only repayment option available to the student loan borrower. As part of this fraudulent process, the student loan borrower is misled to believe that s/he must pay a substantial amount towards their loan in order for the forgiveness process to move forward. However, this is a blatant lie. These funds are actually the third party broker 's fee which this individual has deliberately concealed from the student loan borrower. In short, the student loan borrower is misled to believe that ( 1 ) pursuing student loan forgiveness is their only option to repay their student loan ( 2 ) a payment is required in advance to apply for student loan forgiveness and ( 3 ) that this payment is put towards their student loan when in fact it is a fee to enrich the pocket of the third party broker. 

That said, on XX/XX/year>, I contacted NAVIENT customer service to adjust my long-standing IDR repayment plan as, unfortunately, I was made redundant by my employer on XX/XX/year> and would not be able to make the current payments as I did not have any income. Before contacting NAVIENT, I resubmitted my IDR repayment plan through the Student Aid Gov website, however, as time was of the essence and making sure that a did not default on my student loan, I thought it best to also contact NAVIENT to make sure that they are aware of my unemployment status and confirm that my IDR repayment plan was adjusted accordingly to reflect XXXX income. 

I was connected to whom I believed to be a NAVIENT representative, and explained my change of income circumstances. This individual proceeded to tell me that I needed to pay USD XXXX in order to change my IDR repayment plan so that my payments would go to XXXX. I responded by saying that in the over 25 years of this outstanding student loan that I have never been required to pay a fee to amend my IDR repayment plan. He responded by saying that then there was no guarantee that my IDR repayment would be adjusted to my current income of XXXX. I then requested to speak to a supervisor, and after waiting for almost an hour to no avail, I discontinued the call. 

Thinking that perhaps this NAVIENT representative was mistaken, I immediately called NAVIENT customer service again to speak to a different representative. I was connected to XXXX XXXX, whom I believed was a NAVIENT representative. At no time, during our conversation, did XXXX XXXX identify himself as a third party broker, or state that NAVIENT redirected my call to a third party broker. Again, I informed XXXX XXXX of my unemployment status and that I wanted to adjust my current IDR repayment plan as I would not be able to make the payments. I, also, told XXXX XXXX about my encounter with the previous representative who asked for an upfront payment to adjust my IDR repayment plan. As XXXX XXXX had access to all of my NAVIENT account information, and spoke with authority about my student loan, hence, I assumed XXXX XXXX was a legitimate NAVIENT representative. XXXX XXXX proceeded to tell me that the previous representative did not provide an adequate explanation. And so, with more XXXX salesmanship insisted that I should enter into student loan forgiveness as my loan was over XXXX XXXX XXXX and should have been forgiven a long time ago, and that he was the best person to do this as he has XXXX years of experience. Next, he proceeded to say that I needed to make an upfront payment towards my student loan in the amount of USD XXXX, in order to start this process, and that there was an urgency to do this in order to meet the XX/XX/year> deadline. Thus, I explained to him that I was unemployed and what little savings I had was crucial to my survival until I could find employment. XXXX XXXX persisted that this was the best option and he was advocating in my interest to alleviate my concerns about my student loan repayment. Thus, with much reluctance and dismay taking XXXX XXXX at his word as well as believing that the USD XXXX would go towards my student loan payments for XX/XX/year> and XX/XX/year> so that in XX/XX/year> when the U.S. Department of Education determines who qualifies for student loan forgiveness, I would have completed all of the requirements for student loan forgiveness. Hence, I issued an electronic payment in the amount of USD XXXX through a XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXt XXXX XXXX sent to me via email. Once I completed the PSLF/TEPSLF form and submitted payment, XXXX XXXX instructed me to keep him informed of every correspondence so that he could monitor the student loan forgiveness proceedings. 

On XX/XX/year>, the USD XXXX posted to my checking account. However, when I checked my NAVIENT student loan account payment history, I did not see a record of the USD XXXX. I became concerned that this payment did not appear in my NAVIENT payment history. I contacted XXXX XXXX as to the whereabouts of this payment, and he said that it would appear in XXXX once my NAVIENT student loan was consolidated with the U.S. Department of Education. Once I received confirmation from XXXX of my NAVIENT student loan consolidation with the U.S. Department of Education, I created an account, and much to my dismay, there was not a record of the USD XXXX payment towards my student loan. Extremely distraught, I contacted an XXXX representative and shared the backstory of my student loan forgiveness as well as inquired about the missing USD XXXX payment. The XXXX representative kindly informed me that there is not an upfront payment to apply for student loan forgiveness. The XXXX representative grew concerned that I may have fallen victim to a scam. The XXXX representative escalated an investigation into the missing USD XXXX payment which is still ongoing as of this email correspondence. 

Following my many conversations with several XXXX representatives over several weeks, on XX/XX/year>, I, again, contacted XXXX XXXX, and inquired about the missing USD XXXX payment. Through his continuous deceptive tactics, he said that the USD XXXX payment was part of the consolidation amount and not to worry it was there. I pushed back saying that if this was true then there should be a written record with NAVIENT and XXXX with the USD XXXX reflected in the consolidation. XXXX XXXX continued to try to convince me otherwise. But, I was skeptical of his response. 

Distraught and distressed ever more so, on XX/XX/year>, I contacted XXXX again. I spoke with a representative named XXXX, who kindly reiterated that there is not an upfront payment for consideration by the U.S. Department of Education for student loan forgiveness and that this can be done by any individual for free. She advised that unbeknown to me that I could be dealing with a third party broker as third party brokers request a broker fee to process student loan forgiveness. I told her that I initiated this process through NAVIENT and at no time was I informed of working with a third party broker as I was led to believe that XXXX XXXX was an official NAVIENT representative. 

Desperate for the truth and concern that XXXX XXXX appropriated the USD XXXX for his own personal gain at my expense, I, again, called XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year> and demanded answers about the whereabouts of the USD XXXX, and if he was in fact a third party broker and not a representative of NAVIENT. After many exchanges, XXXX XXXX finally admitted that he was indeed a third party broker explaining that NAVIENT redirects all student loan holders with loans over 20 years directly to third party brokers. Adding insult to injury, XXXX XXXX confessed that the USD XXXX was his broker fee to process and submit my student loan forgiveness application to the U.S. Department of Education.

Profoundly upset and in tears, I said to XXXX XXXX that both he and NAVIENT acted fraudulently forcing me to pay for something that I did not want to pursue in the first place- I contacted NAVIENT with the expressed desire to amend my IDR repayment plan, but instead, XXXX XXXX and NAVIENT had other nefarious intentions. I continued that XXXX XXXX knew that I was unemployed and needed that USD XXXX to pay my bills, keep a roof over my head and survive until I could find employment. I sobbed as I told XXXX XXXX that I was on the verge of losing my home and possessions, and that USD XXXX would be the necessary funds and the only life raft to my imminent survival. XXXX XXXX did not display any empathy, but stood firm in the belief that he did not do any wrong. 

At the conclusion of my conversation with XXXX XXXX, I demanded a refund of the USD XXXX to my account, immediately, along with a written correspondence confirming the refund. He said he would refund my USD XXXX and provide the requested written correspondence, however, with the caveat that he would withdraw my student loan forgiveness application with the U.S. Department of Education.

As of this email correspondence, on XX/XX/year>, I have received neither from XXXX XXXX. And given his duplicity, I do not expect XXXX XXXX to right this wrong and act in good faith. 

Over the last twenty-four hours, I have read countless media reports of NAVIENT 'S XXXX activities with the Federal Trade Commission , U.S. Senators as well as many state Attorney Generals efforts to hold NAVIENT accountable and provide some relief to its innocent victims. I am saddened that even the weight of these governing bodies can not prevent others, such as myself, from falling victim to the predatory student loan industry - An education should not inflict pain and suffering on those trying to build a life. 

As a result of the fraudulent actions of NAVIENT and XXXX XXXX and to prevent this from happening to other innocent student loan borrowers, in reporting this to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, it is my profound hope that you will pursue justice not only for myself, but more importantly, for all who continue to suffer irreparable harm at the hands of those whose self-interest is more important than the greater good. 

Thank you so very much for your kindness and guidance through this incredibly disheartening situation that has left me in a fog of despair. 

If you have additional questions, please contact me as I am happy to provide any additional information. 

With sincere appreciation, XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative:
Experian XXXX Details : Date of First Contact : XX/XX/year> Time of First Contact : XXXX PM Experian XXXX : XXXX Issue : Refusal to Block Fraudulent Credit Card Information Description of the Issue : On XX/XX/year>, at XXXX PM, I contacted Experian to report a credit card that was fraudulently created in my name. This account, which appears to be in collections as of XX/XX/year>, was charged off by the creditor in the amount of {$840.00}. During my conversation with an Experian supervisor named XXXX, I was informed that they would not dispute or remove the fraudulent credit card collection from my credit report because I had not provided them with a police report. Instead, I had submitted a Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) Identity Theft Report. 

To my knowledge, the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) clearly states that a credit reporting agency ( CRA ) is not required to demand a police report to remove fraudulent information from a consumers credit file. An FTC Identity Theft Report should be sufficient for blocking such fraudulent information. Furthermore, Experians own website confirms that reporting identity theft requires a phone call to XXXX, as their online system does not facilitate the process effectively. 

Additionally, I informed the supervisor that I had made numerous previous attempts to report this fraudulent collection, but XXXX customer service number repeatedly blocked me from reporting the identity theft or being transferred to the dispute department. 

After disputing the information with Experian, I received an email requesting extensive documentation, including an identity theft report, government-issued ID, utility bill, and more. I provided all the requested information. 

However, on XX/XX/year>, at XXXX AM, I received an email from Experian stating the following : XXXX XXXX XXXX, We are responding to your request that information in your personal credit report be blocked due to identity theft. Based on our review of your request and the information available to us, we have determined that either : Your request to block was made in error, XXXX, your request to block information was based on a material misrepresentation, XXXX, you knowingly obtained or should have known that you obtained possession of goods, services, or moneys as a result of XXXX or more of the transactions that you are seeking to block. 

Therefore, we are declining your request to block XXXX or more of the items of information. If you have additional relevant information that indicates that the disputed item ( XXXX ) resulted from identity theft, please contact us again and provide this information. If you still believe the disputed item ( XXXX ) is inaccurate, then we will add a statement of continued dispute to the credit report at your request. 

To view your rights, visit www.experian.com/fraudrights and www.experian.com/fcra. 

Experian then insisted that I provide additional documentation to validate the identity theft report, specifically asking for evidence that the report was filed with a federal, state, or local law enforcement agency. This request contradicts the FCRAs provisions, which state that an FTC Identity Theft Report should be sufficient for blocking fraudulent information from a consumers credit report. 

Potential Violations by Experian : 1. Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), Section 605B ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ) : Experian is required to block fraudulent information on a consumers credit report if an identity theft report is provided. The law does not specifically mandate a police report, and an FTC Identity Theft Report should be adequate. 
Experians refusal to block the fraudulent credit card account, despite receiving an FTC Identity Theft Report, is a direct violation of this section.

2. Failure to Investigate ( FCRA Section 611 ) : The FCRA obligates credit reporting agencies to investigate disputes about the accuracy of information in a consumers credit report. Experians refusal to investigate or remove the fraudulent information without a police report, despite having an FTC Identity Theft Report, could be a failure to fulfill their obligation under the FCRA.

3. Misleading and Unreasonable Documentation Requirements : Experians insistence on a police report and additional documentation, despite the FCRAs provisions, may constitute unreasonable documentation requirements, further violating consumer protection laws.

Resolution Requested : I request that the CFPB investigate Experians practices and enforce compliance with the FCRA. Specifically, I ask that Experian : XXXX. Immediately block and remove the fraudulent credit card collection account from my credit report. 
XXXX. Cease demanding unnecessary documentation, such as a police report, when an FTC Identity Theft Report has been provided. 
XXXX Review and correct their dispute-handling procedures to ensure compliance with federal laws and regulations. 

This fraudulent account should not be on my credit file, as it was created without my consent, and I have never interacted with the creditor or collection agency associated with this account.

- **Delay in Resolution : ** By not acting promptly to block the fraudulent information, TransUnion is also violating California state laws designed to protect consumers from identity theft and its damaging effects.

5. **Californias Unfair Competition Law ( UCL ) - Business & Professions Code 17200 : ** - **Violation : ** The actions of TransUnion may also constitute unfair business practices under Californias UCL , which prohibits unlawful, unfair, or fraudulent business acts or practices.

- **Intentional Hardship : ** TransUnions failure to comply with legal obligations and its misrepresentation of documentation create an unfair and unlawful barrier to resolving this issue, furthering the hardship I experience.

15 USC 1681 ( FCRA section 604 a section 2 ) states that " In general. '' I DID NOT give these companies written authorization to access my credit report or furnish my personal information. They do not have my written authorization granting Permissible Purpose to make inquiries to access my consumer report.

Any and all consent to the financial institutions listed below whether it be verbal, non-verbal, written, implied or otherwise is revoked. 

15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ) states that " A financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party unless the consumer is given an explanation of how the consumer can exercise that nondisclosure option. '' I never gave the financial institutions listed below written authorization and furthermore they have never given me a notice of my right to exercise my right to opt out. 

Not only that 15 USC 1681c ( a ) ( 5 ) states " Except as authorized under subsection ( b ), no consumer reporting agency may make any consumer report containing any of the following items of information : Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years. '' These inquiries are adverse items reporting without my permission which is against the law.

15 U.S. Code 1681e states Every consumer reporting agency shall maintain reasonable procedures designed to avoid violations of section 1681c of this title and to limit the furnishing of consumer reports to the purposes listed under section 1681b of this title. The CRAs are not following federal law and procedures. Furthermore, There is no law in existence that grants a financial institution the right to report any information on a private citizens consumer report but consumers have a right to opt out and CRAs have a duty to follow procedures of the FCRA, The Privacy Act and other federal laws. 12 CFR 1016.7 states that " A consumer may exercise the right to opt out at any time. The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act ( FERPA ) is a federal law that was enacted in 1974 to protect the privacy of student education records. FERPA applies to all public and private schools, as well as any state or local education agencies that receive funding from the US Department of Education. The law has been amended seven times since its enactment. 
FERPA protects the privacy of students and parents by limiting the disclosure of personally identifiable information from education records. This includes records, files, documents, films, tapes, and photographs. FERPA gives parents certain rights regarding their children 's education records, such as : Inspecting and reviewing records Requesting that records be corrected Having a formal hearing if the school refuses to amend the record Placing a statement with the record When a student turns XXXX or enters a postsecondary institution, their rights under FERPA transfer to them. Students can see everything in their educational records, except for information about other students, financial records of parents, and confidential letters of recommendation.

I was contacted by Chase Bank by letter that they had determined that my condominium address is in a flood zone, and therefore, I must buy flood insurance to protect their interest in the condo unit. Oddly, they also wrote that FEMA determined my home was in a flood zone.

If I did not purchase flood insurance for them, they would do so for me and pass the costs on to me by raising my mortgage. They then wrote that if I believe I'm not in a flood zone, to contact FEMA and to request an amendment or revision to the flood map ( XXXX or XXXX ) and that I would have to pay for any costs associated with getting them to revise the map and send proof. I went to the FEMA website, entered my address and it showed that I was NOT in a flood zone as of XX/XX/year>. So I'm not sure what they are supposed to revise or amend. 

I called Chase to get more information and the person I spoke to reiterated that FEMA made this determination. I point her to the FEMA website and she said she was not sure how to read the map. She asked me to contact FEMA and to go through the XXXX process. 

I called FEMA and the person I spoke to said ( 1 ) that FEMA does not communicate with banks about flood map updates, and ( 2 ) Chase bank has a third party they contract with that makes the " Standard Flood Hazard Determinations '' ... or something like that. This XXXX representative then went to their maps and confirmed that my home is not in a flood zone. I asked XXXX what to do and they recommended doing both of the following actions : ( 1 ) Go through the XXXX process but that it takes 60 days ; ( 2 ) File a complaint with the regulatory body over the organization that Chase contracts with to make the determinations, and to contact the state attorney general. FEMA gave me a number to call. 

I called that number, went through a long menu of option, spoke to someone who then told me that it does sound like Chase is engaged in forced-insurance. She then said the best entity to help me through this is the Consumer Finance Protection Bureau.

I decided to contact Chase one more time. I explained the situation, and relayed to them what FEMA said and that FEMA denies communicating with them directly ( contradicting what the previous Chase representative said ). This new Chase rep admits that it was another entity that makes that determination, and reiterated the only remedy available to me is to fill out the XXXX forms at my expense. She also reiterated that if I don't buy a flood insurance policy for Chase, they would do it for me, and pass the costs to me, even though it'll take 2 months before FEMA can send proof that I'm not in a flood zone. She mentioned something about offering a refund if they were wrong, but that seems to contradict aspects of what is written in the letter, particularly where there's a gap in coverage.

In short, as best as I understand it, Chase contracts with some 3rd Party to make determinations about whether a property is in a flood zone, then Chase claims that it was FEMA who made that determination, then demands homeowners to buy flood insurance to protect Chase 's interest in the property. If the homeowner doesn't comply, Chase will buy what they openly admit may not be the most affordable insurance. To comply with their demand, they give homeowners LESS than the 60 days it takes to go through the XXXX process ( which you may have to pay for ) to prove you are not in the flood zone, even though ANYONE can simply go to the FEMA website, enter their address, and see that they are not in a flood zone. 

I did a quick XXXX search and it seems Chase has a history of doing this. 

This is not at all fair.

To prepare me for college, my parents gave me blank checks for me to deposit once I opened a bank account in America. They were blank checks because they were unsure of the amount I would need and told me to write the amount myself after I confirmed with them. And checks can be deposited immediately while international wire transfer might take awhile to send. 
On XX/XX/year>, I wrote and deposited a check for {$2200.00} as that was the allowance my parents were giving me for the school year. The check went through and the money was transferred from their account to mine. Both of our accounts are from CHASE. They used to live in the USA, and had remaining funds in their account, which is why they told me to take the money from their CHASE account. However, I received a notice XXXX days later that my account had been restricted. I have since been unable to use any of the funds in my account, including funds not associated with the check I deposited. 
I went to CHASE and asked if there was a way to lift the restriction. They told me the reason they restricted my account was because my handwriting did not match my parents. We were unaware that this would cause a problem because this method has worked before ( blank checks deposited being written by another person ). So they told me the only way to lift the restriction was for my parents to verify that the check was real. The only ways to verify are either that they go to a branch near them, or CHASE will reach out to them through a verified phone number. They are unable to go to a physical branch because they are not in the USA. Additionally, CHASE does not make international phone calls. I have asked if there is any other way to verify that the check is real ( email, social security number, ID, etc. ). They have adamantly told me no. 
However, the bank has already taken the money out of my parents account. They did not wait to verify the check first before they transferred the money. They have transferred it into my account and suspended the funds indefinitely. The only way for the money to be used again is for my parents to verify it. And if my account stays restricted, CHASE is telling me that they may close it soon. They will send me a check for the remaining funds in my account that are not associated with the check, but the {$2200.00} they will keep hold of until it is verified. 
We have been calling them for almost XXXX weeks now and have gotten absolutely nowhere. We have tried to create a new US phone number for my parents and have registered it to their CHASE account. But when we ask if that number can be used for verification, CHASE tells us it is not a verified phone number. It fails their risk program every time. The name that comes up with the number apparently does not match my parents. They advised us to contact our service provider and have them update the information. We did exactly that, and our service provider told us the information was updated and we could call the bank again. They confirmed multiple times that the information had been updated. However, after calling the bank, they told us that it still does not work. So as of now, I am unable to use any of my funds, and my parents lost out on {$2200.00}. It would make sense if CHASE tried to verify the check before they took the money out of my parents account, but they did not. They took the money out and suspended it, and my parents are unable to get it back. We have called dozens and dozens of times and different people tell us different things each time but the gist of it is that the money cant be used by anyone unless its through a verified phone number, and the phone number we gave them is not verified. I myself have gone to a physical branch to ask if theres something they can do and the workers there are clueless.

Inaccurate Addresses : My credit report includes addresses where I have never lived.

Specifically : Violation of FCRA Section 605 ( a ) [ 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( a ) ] : This section prohibits credit reporting agencies from reporting inaccurate or outdated information. The presence of incorrect names, addresses, unauthorized accounts, and inquiries on my credit report is a direct violation of this provision.

Violation of FCRA Section 611 [ 15 U.S.C. 1681i ] : This section requires credit reporting agencies to investigate and correct inaccurate information when a consumer disputes the accuracy of information on their credit report. The failure to remove these inaccuracies after my disputes were raised is a violation of this section. 

Violation of FCRA Section 623 [ 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ] : This section imposes a duty on furnishers of information ( like creditors ) to provide accurate information to credit reporting agencies and to correct and update information when they know or have reason to believe it is inaccurate. The continued reporting of unauthorized accounts and inquiries violates this section. 

The continued reporting of this inaccurate information is causing significant harm to my creditworthiness.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On Thursday, XX/XX/XXXX, I was notified via a text message from Capital One that they blocked a transaction for about {$1000.00} from XXXX as it was flagged as possible fraud. The transaction was indeed fraudulent and was the last of a number of attempts in the month of XXXX to utilize my debit card without my consent. The text message from Capital one instructed me to call their fraud hotline with my case number. I did so at XXXX that day once it opened. 

I was supposed to travel out of state that day- my train was to depart the station at noon. As I do not have access to significant lines of credit, if I didn't have my debit card, I was not going to be able to fund my travel. I called Capital One at the number provided, provided the case number, confirmed the activity was fraudulent, and asked for options for quickest resolution possible as I was due to leave the state that day. I asked if there was an option to unfreeze the card and accept liability for any fraudulent use- my hope was that i could utilize the lock/unlock card feature in the Capital One app to use my card for my own purchases during my weekend of travel. The customer service representative told me this was not possible and that my only remedy was to either to go a branch to take out cash every time I needed to use money for the weekend, or wait for the card to come in the mail. They told me that the debit card was " already cancelled '' and there was no ability to utilize it for purchases once cancelled. They told me the account was also " restricted '' but were not able to give me a clear understanding of what that meant. I was told the card would be expedited in the mail and that I would receive it within three business days. Due to these issues, I decided not to travel that weekend and await my new card in the mail. 

By Friday, XX/XX/XXXX, over a week later and well past the three business days they told me it would take, I called Capital One again. They told me that I " refused '' authorization to cancel the card and therefore they did not mail me a new debit card. At this point, it is the end of the month, and there are bills I have to pay that rely on my debit card as they don't have an option for me to pay by account transfer through a routing number. I am a doctoral student and needed to be able to order my textbooks for the semester that had started that week. I was told that if i was now " able to authorize '' the cancellation, they would process the card and it would ship, again, in 3-4 business days. Due to the fact that it is a bank holiday on Monday, that means my card is estimated to be here next Friday, XX/XX/XXXX. They would not transfer me beyond one manager higher than the initial customer service representative that I spoke to.

Two hours later, I received a call from someone in the dispute resolution department at Capital One who told me they reviewed the calls and found " no malice '' and that the fact that I ended the call without authorizing a new card to be sent to me ( I was unaware they needed more authorization - I had provided all my verification info including name, address, phone number, SSN, date of last transaction, card number, account number and was told the only remedy was a new card, so I assumed a new card had been issued ) that this was my fault and the only remedy would be to wait another week for a card to arrive in the mail. I asked for another remedy and was told there are no other remedies. I said that while I can own that I was frustrated in my initial conversations with Capital One, I felt the lack of communication from the customer service agents on the process was the key issue, as they did not tell me they required my explicit authorization to mail a new debit card. Of course I needed a new debit card- they had cancelled mine! I felt that went without saying, especially given the subjective nature of the conversation where I made it clear that I needed a debit card in order to make purchases. 

I asked numerous times for someone to speak to regarding the experience with customer service - because of their inability to understand my concern, they forced me into a position to accrue interest on my one line of credit, incur fees on bills that required a debit card for payment or force me into a position to pay credit card fees to put them on a line of credit. Either way, I'm out more money because of Capital One 's negligence and inability to rectify this issue. The fact that all operations are offshore forces customers into financially challenging positions due to their inability to expedite any concern from XXXX soil or from a branch location. I live in a major city - I should be able to rectify the majority of my banking issues in-person at a branch. I even asked if I could pick a card up at the branch, and would go out of my way to go get it if it meant saving a day in the timeline so that I could pay my bills. Capital One was unable to accommodate me in any way and forced me to be without a debit card for two weeks. I've incurred interest on my credit cards, been unable to pay bills, had subscriptions connected to my debit account turned off, all because Capital One did not send me a new card.
